{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZf0zfw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDG_UA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 53, "title": "Correct WD2793 Type-I readiness and verification sequencing", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `21f003b457203e5dca831c86a759eef8bfb3b51d`, `crates/msx-core/src/disk.rs:310,486` rejects or aborts Type-I commands when READY is low. Side/drive/motor writes also abort them. `finish_movement()` at line 363 immediately evaluates a track/geometry predicate instead of scheduling verification.

Consequently, firmware cannot perform normal diskless positioning, and polling observes premature completion or errors. Simply removing READY checks would also let absent-drive commands move A:'s head and report A:'s track-zero sensor. No particular commercial-game failure is established.

## Expected outcome

Execute RESTORE, SEEK and STEP-family commands independently of READY, route their pulses and feedback through the selected drive, and implement distinct movement, settling and verification phases. Both Weave and Philips interfaces must observe the corrected shared controller.

## Context

[Issue #47](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/47) and [PR #48](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/48) corrected incremental movement while explicitly deferring this work. Open Issue/PR inspection returned none.

Inspected references:

- [TI second-source TMS279X/WD279X manual](https://deramp.com/swtpc.com/DC_5/TMS279X_DataSheet.pdf), printed pages 3, 9, 12–13 and 17: READY-independent Type I, 30 ms verification settling at 1 MHz, matching-track/good-CRC ID search, five-revolution failure limit and RESTORE failure after 255 unsuccessful pulses. This is an edited manufacturer transcription; physical WD2793 confirmation remains unavailable. Text was readable; the screenshot attempt failed.
- [Pinned openMSX WD2793](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/WD2793.cc): movement scheduling and an HLT-high MSX assumption. Its verification remains TODO, so it is not a verification oracle.
- Pinned [drive multiplexer](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/DriveMultiplexer.cc), [dummy drive](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/DiskDrive.cc) and [real drive](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/RealDrive.cc): selected-drive routing, absent-drive feedback and media/motor-dependent index pulses. Track-zero wiring varies by machine.

Raw DSK contains sector payloads, not physical ID/gap timing. Use an explicitly documented normal-track approximation. Preserve the existing motor-independent track-zero policy for installed A; do not claim universal physical wiring. Prior WD-manual access limitations remain unresolved.

Native movement/verification tests and CPU/browser Philips fixtures are present. [Existing CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40027778363/job/120668178996) report 206 Rust and 110 browser passes, including existing disk cases. Those tests validate the earlier contract, not the proposed phases. No application checks were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Remove READY gating from Type-I command acceptance and progress. READY remains live status bit 7; sector-command readiness and write safety remain unchanged. Motor/side/drive control writes must not terminate Type I merely because READY changes. Preserve explicit mount/eject/reset/interface-removal cancellation boundaries.
- [ ] Separate controller register sequencing from drive mechanics. Only selected installed A receives physical steps; absent B/no-drive cannot move A or expose its sensors. Route relevant Type-I drive status consistently with selection, including Philips reset-latch selection. Preserve remembered direction, T updates, completed movement and the documented upper-stop policy. An absent track-zero signal must make RESTORE terminate with seek error after 255 unsuccessful pulses.
- [ ] V=0 retains existing movement completion timing. V=1, including a no-step SEEK or already-zero RESTORE, remains BUSY through an additional 30 ms settling phase and subsequent ID search under an explicit HLT-high assumption. DRQ stays clear; IRQ rises only at completion. Keep live not-ready distinct from seek error.
- [ ] Define deterministic nine-sector, good-CRC synthetic IDs for each supported raw track/side at the existing 300 rpm profile. Publish ID positions, index phase, rounding and boundary ordering. Verification succeeds upon encountering a matching cylinder ID, independently of the Sector register or payload contents. Missing sides or mismatched cylinders search until the five-revolution/index-event limit. Do not invent CRC faults from payload bytes. Without index/ID input, retain a cancellable BUSY search rather than fabricate elapsed revolutions; document this selected-model inference.
- [ ] Consume elapsed movement, settling, ID and index events chronologically across large ticks, preserving fractional deadlines. Results must agree for large, irregular and single-cycle partitions. FORCE INTERRUPT/reset must cancel every phase without later resurrection or lost completed movement; retain existing interface signal polarity and acknowledgement behavior.
- [ ] Add independently calculated register traces covering all Type-I families, both V values, no-step cases, all step rates, track mismatch, both geometries, missing side, diskless/motor-off A, absent B/no-drive, selection changes and RESTORE exhaustion. Check immediately before/at/after settling, ID and timeout events, including ticks spanning multiple revolutions. Infer A's retained position through later sector access. Replace obsolete Type-I abort/immediate-verification assertions while preserving sector-abort, partial-write and dirty-media regressions. Record meaningful baseline failures and corrected results.
- [ ] Extend original CPU-executed Philips fixtures on both models to observe diskless positioning and delayed verification through ordinary register polling. Exercise compiled Wasm at `/` and `/msx-rust/`, with independently expected trace/output results. Preserve MSX1/MSX2 video/input, PSG/SCC audio, firmware/sub-ROM/mapper coexistence, SRAM persistence, private disk ownership/export and fixture provenance. No proprietary firmware, BIOS traps or gameplay prerequisite.
- [ ] Update `docs/disks.md` and affected documentation. Keep full HLD/status-bit-5 lifecycle, physical spin-up, flux/CRC anomalies, sector-transfer timing and additional commands explicitly separate. The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using README setup as needed. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings before merge; distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Compare original movement/selection traces with pinned upstream behavior, excluding its unimplemented verification. Record additional software checks using already lawfully available inputs separately. Authored diagnostics do not establish commercial compatibility; physical hardware and human gameplay are unnecessary for acceptance.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
